investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), indicating no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free slots. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: Scheduler returned 'Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 142s before the eval timed out.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: Contract gap confirms orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState were never written, meaning createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a schedulable VM.

sibling.remote-agent-state: Identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 144s — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across a second independent probe attempt.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: Identical scheduler error, pod stuck 147s — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across a third independent probe attempt spanning roughly 7.5 minutes total (09:52–10:00 UTC).

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147814 (~147s), which is below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms but the check still failed because the pod never became schedulable, not because of a latency breach.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: Runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; the pod scheduling failure upstream of this call prevents any evidence from being written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: Contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the VM was never allocated.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes in the production-api cluster. All three sibling checks hit the same error across ~7.5 minutes, ruling out a transient single-pod race condition.

[Medium confidence] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes have a fixed or misconfigured kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit that has not been scaled to meet current demand.

[Medium confidence] A concurrent workload or a leaked/stuck peer-pod VM from a previous eval run is holding the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes, preventing new allocations. The preemption check found no victims, which is consistent with all slots being held by non-preemptible pods.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods may be overly restrictive, excluding 4 of 6 nodes that could otherwise provide kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity if the selector were broadened.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling misconfiguration would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create eval passed on a concurrent or immediately subsequent run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the pod's node affinity/selector were found to be misconfigured (e.g., targeting a node label that no longer exists), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a selector mismatch, and the kata.peerpods.io/vm insufficiency would be a secondary symptom.

If a different feature's checks (e.g., local-agent-create) also failed at the same time with unrelated errors, it could indicate a broader cluster or API availability issue rather than a resource-specific constraint.

If the eval runner's access token was invalid or expired, the probe would have returned a SKIP status (per line 1882 of run-status-probes.mjs) rather than a scheduling error, so a token problem is already ruled out by the presence of the scheduler message.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-26T09:55–10:00Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with a complete evidence gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible regardless of preemption. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims found, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–147 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks impossible. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing agent pods or leaked/zombie pods that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are also the ones with the exhausted VM quota, creating a double constraint with no escape hatch.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, and the total VM quota on those nodes is too small for concurrent eval runs plus any production workload sharing the same nodes.

QUATERNARY — leaked agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs): if cleanup failed in a previous run, orphaned pods could be holding VM slots, reducing available capacity to zero.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), indicating no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free slots. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: Scheduler returned 'Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 142s before the eval timed out.

failed-check.evidence: Evidence object is empty ({}); all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the agent pod never reaching a running state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: Contract gap confirms orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState were never written, meaning createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a schedulable VM.

sibling.remote-agent-state: Identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 144s — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across a second independent probe attempt.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: Identical scheduler error, pod stuck 147s — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across a third independent probe attempt spanning roughly 7.5 minutes total (09:52–10:00 UTC).

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147814 (~147s), which is below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms but the check still failed because the pod never became schedulable, not because of a latency breach.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: Runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; the pod scheduling failure upstream of this call prevents any evidence from being written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: Contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the VM was never allocated.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes in the production-api cluster. All three sibling checks hit the same error across ~7.5 minutes, ruling out a transient single-pod race condition.

[Medium confidence] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes have a fixed or misconfigured kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit that has not been scaled to meet current demand.

[Medium confidence] A concurrent workload or a leaked/stuck peer-pod VM from a previous eval run is holding the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes, preventing new allocations. The preemption check found no victims, which is consistent with all slots being held by non-preemptible pods.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods may be overly restrictive, excluding 4 of 6 nodes that could otherwise provide kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity if the selector were broadened.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-26T09:55–10:00Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with a complete evidence gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible regardless of preemption. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims found, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–147 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks impossible. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing agent pods or leaked/zombie pods that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are also the ones with the exhausted VM quota, creating a double constraint with no escape hatch.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, and the total VM quota on those nodes is too small for concurrent eval runs plus any production workload sharing the same nodes.

QUATERNARY — leaked agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs): if cleanup failed in a previous run, orphaned pods could be holding VM slots, reducing available capacity to zero.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > requested on the 2 eligible nodes), the resource-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a scheduler bug.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector were found to be misconfigured to target zero nodes (rather than the 2 kata-capable nodes), the primary cause would be affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after clearing any leaked pods succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, that would confirm leaked pods as the primary cause rather than a structural capacity shortfall.

If the cluster were found to have more than 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource (contradicting the scheduler message), the scheduler message itself would need re-examination for a different root cause.

If no pods were found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a transient scheduler or admission-controller error would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and surfaces a warning if available slots fall below a minimum threshold.

Add a cluster-capacity eval that independently monitors the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource utilization rate and alerts when utilization exceeds a configurable high-water mark (e.g., 80%), decoupled from the agent lifecycle checks.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes beyond the eval timeout) and flags them as cleanup failures.

Consider adding a node-affinity validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes (currently 2) match the agent pod's affinity/selector before each eval run, catching affinity drift independently of scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 09:55 and 10:00 UTC on 2026-06-26 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. This prevents any new remote-agent pod from being scheduled. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment and is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, confirming no lower-priority pods are available to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's node affinity or selector rules exclude 4 of 6 nodes from consideration entirely, artificially constraining scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or stale, capacity could appear exhausted even if other nodes could theoretically host the workload.

TERTIARY — Cluster node count insufficient for current remote-agent demand: the cluster has only 6 nodes total, 2 of which carry kata.peerpods.io/vm. If concurrent eval runs or production workloads have saturated those 2 nodes, no headroom remains for the observability probe pods.

LOWER — Transient spike in remote-agent pod creation (e.g., from other eval runs or user activity) that temporarily exhausted VM slots at the time of the eval window (09:55–10:00 UTC); slots may have freed up after the eval timed out.

reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Observe whether the pod scheduling error recurs or the check passes.

reproductionSteps.details: Query the Kubernetes cluster for allocatable and allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on all nodes to determine current headroom. Identify which pods are consuming the slots on the 2 eligible nodes.

reproductionSteps.label: Review the pod's node affinity and selector rules
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the pod spec submitted by createAgent for the 'remote' type to understand why 4 of 6 nodes are excluded. Determine whether the affinity rules are intentional or overly restrictive.

affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agent eval checks failed with the same Kubernetes Unschedulable event citing exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — eval runner createAgent call
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which submits the pod that failed to schedule. Zero evidence was returned because this step never completed (failed-check.evidence, source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

affectedAreas.reason: The remote-agents feature has degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (line 187-188). With all 3 checks failing, the feature is at or beyond the outage threshold per its registry configuration (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster for current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource availability on all 6 nodes to determine whether slots are still exhausted or have freed up since the eval run at 09:55–10:00 UTC.
Identify and review pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes; determine if any are leaked, stuck, or from prior eval runs that did not clean up.

Review the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional; if not, correcting the affinity rules would expand the schedulable node pool.
Consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes or adding additional kata-capable nodes to the cluster if demand consistently exceeds current capacity.
Re-run the three failing eval checks after any remediation to confirm recovery and collect the expected evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

Review whether the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is reliably releasing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after each probe run to prevent slot leakage across eval cycles.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether all three checks fail consistently with the same scheduling error, reinforcing the shared infrastructure dependency diagnosis (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a subsequent eval run of remote-agent-runtime passes and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (temporary VM slot exhaustion) rather than a persistent capacity deficit.
If kubectl or equivalent cluster inspection shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of re-inspection, the exhaustion was temporary and has since resolved.

If the pod's node affinity rules are found to be intentionally restrictive and the 4 excluded nodes are confirmed to be ineligible by design (e.g., wrong architecture or zone), then the root cause is purely VM slot exhaustion on the 2 correct nodes, not a misconfiguration.

If the local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime sibling checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) are found to be passing in the same run window, that would confirm the failure is specific to the kata peer-pod scheduling layer and not a broader API or authentication issue.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node label or resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on the cluster nodes and warns when headroom falls below a defined threshold, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that fires a warning if a remote-agent pod takes longer than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s) to reach the Running state, catching capacity pressure before it causes full scheduling failures.

Add a cluster node affinity validation eval that confirms the remote-agent pod's node selector and affinity rules match at least N schedulable nodes, catching misconfiguration before it causes Unschedulable events.
Consider a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval cycle, ensuring VM slots are not leaked between runs.
